- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% of spike magnitude.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 30d), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of bullish sentiment.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% under), sentiment is often bearish — increase forecast by 1–3% per day of bearish sentiment.
- Mean reversion is common in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is 5–10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often misses mid-term trend — use 14-day moving average as anchor for correction.
